name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.29.0 — a derived session queue closes the 2026-08-18-style "reconstruct the ordering by hand" session (specs/20260823/08): `spec-queue.json`, one file in the git common directory (`git -C <root> rev-parse --git-common-dir`, a relative result resolved against `<root>`; shared by every linked worktree, invisible to `git status`), stores JJ's intended work order across briefs plus free-text prompt items and their done-when predicates (closed vocabulary D5: `brief-state`, `spec-exists`, `ledger-count` with a `baseline` stamp, `manual`). New `spec-queue.js` (subcommands `next add bump defer done list ok hello`, exposed as `/spec:queue`) owns every write: reconcile-on-invocation (D6) inserts an on-disk brief missing from the queue right after its `Depends on:`/letter-suffix parent with an `auto_placed` stamp that only `bump`/`defer`/`done`/`ok` clears, and seeding (D7 — absent/empty file, an explicit write subcommand only, never the hook) fills all non-done briefs in roadmap order with zero stamps and one summary line. `spec-status.js` stays the sole `--next` derivation surface (D2 — every live consumer shells its stdout verbatim, and the one `--json` consumer, autopilot, was deleted 2026-08-18): the queue is a read-only overlay inside `deriveNext()` — queue position orders unblocked entries across briefs, deliberately overriding cross-brief closest-to-done ranking; prompt items surface verbatim with no `@path` suffix; `/spec:escape` red-observation entries keep rank −3 supremacy over every queue position (D10); a linked worktree suppresses the overlay entirely (D9 — the global pointer misleads mid-spec). No queue file means `--next` is byte-identical to today (D1–D3). A new SessionStart hook (matcher `startup|resume|clear` — D8 deliberately excludes `compact`/`fork`, mid-task refresh not a fresh session) runs a thin bash guard (`session-queue.sh`, zero node-startup cost when no queue file exists) that prints the top item's paste line plus one veto notice per un-cleared `auto_placed` item in the main checkout, or a finish-this-tree line inside a linked worktree; an empty queue with no notices prints nothing. New `/spec:status` anomaly kinds `queue-auto-placed` (names the veto command) and `queue-orphan` (a queued brief with no matching file) join the existing anomaly narration. Deviation: D12 named 7.28.0 as the bump target, but a concurrent same-day incident fix had already claimed it at HEAD by build time — per this repo's own next-free-version Gotcha this lands at 7.29.0 instead, recorded in the spec's deviations sidecar. 7.28.0 — prose-cap.js's entry regex is broadened from a bullet that must OPEN with a bracket tag (backtick-wrapped or bare) to any top-level `- ` bullet, closing a fail-open found 2026-08-23: real hosts write the `[host]`/`[plugin]` tag at the END of the entry, so Upwell's `.claude/rules/spec-pipeline.md` held 138 Gotchas entries of which 0 matched — the cap had never fired there and nothing was ever evicted — while this repo's own tag-first file kept the live-file suite test green (authored ≠ activated; second recorded member of the silent-matcher fail-open class after the AC-ID prefix-collision coverage fail-open of 2026-08-22). No doctrine ever mandated tag position; the new shape is the same top-level-bullet count the review driver's sidecar grammar and build.md's ledger count already use, indented continuation lines still never count, and overcounting only fires the cap early where a human judges at fold time. Same-day incident fix per core § Incident Policy: regex + script-header history, tag-at-end regression and deliberate-trip tests, specs/20260823/06's Contracts amended in place; spec-review-driver.js's strict flush-left sidecar grammar is deliberately untouched (JJ ruling 2026-08-23). 7.27.0 — the deviations sidecar (`<spec>.deviations.md`) moves from pure convention to backstop enforcement inside `spec-review-driver.js`'s existing machinery, closing specs/20260823/07: a skipped fold or a count-invisible entry now surfaces as a driver refusal with a named remedy, never a silent loss. (1) The driver validates the sidecar against a bullets-only entry grammar (blank / `#`-prefixed / `- ` bullet / indented continuation of an open entry; anything else is malformed) whenever it derives state, and persists the observation (`entries`, `malformed`) into the review sidecar on every derivation while the file exists on disk. (2) The CLOSE step's printed fold instruction now enumerates every entry (numbered, 120-char-bounded first line) ahead of the fold, so the folding session sees the full content in the instruction channel. (3) `--mark closed` gains two refusals, both exit 2 with a named remedy and state left unchanged: the sidecar still exists on disk (fold not done), or it was deleted but the last persisted observation records one or more malformed lines (restore-and-repair remedy naming `git checkout <ref> -- <path>`). No new review leg, script, or ledger field: fold outcome stays a session judgment, and the build row's `deviations` count remains the cross-spec signal.
